testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you go downhill and speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going downhill
questions.explanation: Always slow down and shift to a lower gear before going down a hill. If you don't start down a hill slowly enough, your brakes may overheat and stop working properly.

questions.question: If you have more than one driver's license:

options.text: You can get caught through a shared computer system between states.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can get caught through a shared computer system between states.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to prevent one person from getting multiple licenses. It is illegal to have more than one driver's license.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo moving forward
Protect the driver's head when getting into a truck cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo moving forward
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: What is a problem with retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed everywhere

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed everywhere
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, retarders can be loud and are not permitted in all areas.

questions.question: When a vehicle is loaded with too much cargo:

options.text: It usually does not affect the vehicle
It can affect steering and brake control
It can affect the electrical system

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect steering and brake control
questions.explanation: Overloading a vehicle harms steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to recognize when cargo is too heavy or poorly balanced.

questions.question: How should you perform pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items
The same way each time so you don't forget anything

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This consistency helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed for a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. No matter the cargo size, always use at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: How often should you inspect cargo during a trip?

options.text: Only at the start of the drive
Only after driving a long distance

questions.correctAnswerText: After every break
questions.explanation: Check cargo and tie-downs before starting. During the trip, inspect them within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts usually means they are loose. If you see rust near wheel nuts, check if they are tight before you drive.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity
They usually have high centers of gravity
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and the load can shift while driving.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts could be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check if the nuts are tight when you see rust.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks do not have the ability to move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, the posted speed:

options.text: May be exceeded if passing another vehicle.
May be exceeded if driving in a rural area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be exceeded.
questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the maximum speed under ideal conditions. Slow down as road conditions require. Never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: A driver may have:

options.text: An automobile license from one state and a CDL from another.
Two licenses: one for automobiles and one for trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only one license.
questions.explanation: A person can have only one license. Having more than one license can result in jail time and fines up to $5,000.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirrors on the driver's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors often. Use a helper whenever possible.

questions.question: Scan the road ____ ahead of your vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds
questions.explanation: Good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This lets you spot hazards early and react. Look for vehicles entering the highway or changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign that brakes will need repair?

options.text: Brake pads are not covered in grease.
Brake pads are not covered in oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes are worn thin.
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are broken or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: Looking far ahead of your vehicle while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged, as there is little you can do about something far up the road.
Encouraged to help you identify hazards as early as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged to help you identify hazards as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This helps you spot hazards early so you have time to respond.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, but have the brakes repaired within a week.
Pull over and inspect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and inspect the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely right away. Inspect and repair the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a CMV illegal?

options.text: No, it is okay on rural roads.
No, it is okay when contacting your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and illegal for CMV drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver on the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from them.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance from distracted drivers. Stay back and give them plenty of space.

questions.question: What must you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?
questions.correctAnswerText: Always use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you NOT do during an engine compartment inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: During an engine inspection, check oil and coolant levels. Do not drain brake fluid.

questions.question: When should manual air tank drains be opened?

options.text: They should be sealed with glue.

questions.correctAnswerText: After each day of driving.
questions.explanation: Open manual air tank drains daily to remove water and oil that can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: CMVs must have emergency equipment including spare fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Gives you more control while braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you more control while braking hard.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control during hard braking. It does not always make the vehicle stop shorter.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Push in the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is almost at idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
questions.explanation: To stop smoothly, apply steady brake pressure. For manual transmissions, push in the clutch as the engine nears idle.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: Wait for the state to notify your employer.
Tell your employer within two business days.
Tell your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, or canceled.

questions.question: When should you sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After defects are fixed or certified as not needing repair
After each time you fill up with fuel

questions.correctAnswerText: After defects are fixed or certified as not needing repair
questions.explanation: Sign the inspection report only if defects were found and either fixed or confirmed they do not need repair.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible on the axles.
Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
Not worry about how the cargo weight is spread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
questions.explanation: When loading cargo, the weight on each axle should not be too light or too heavy. Bad loading can cause steering problems, reduce tire grip, or damage the axles.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.correctAnswerText: Lower
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you go downhill.

questions.question: Without enough oil in the engine:

options.text: A vehicle will have trouble stopping.
A vehicle will jerk and shake while driving.
The engine may be damaged quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine may be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine needs enough oil pressure to work properly. An engine can be destroyed very fast if it runs without oil.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:

options.text: Checked to make sure they are tight.
Checked only about once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked to make sure they are tight.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, inspect all belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: When driving in hot weather:

options.text: Air pressure in tires will go down.
Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: Check tire pressure in hot weather because air expands in heat and increases pressure. To prevent overheating, the engine needs enough oil and enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system. Antifreeze is important for both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators are:

options.text: Used to add alcohol to air brake systems.
Only allowed in the north part of the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used to add alcohol to air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. They add alcohol to the braking system to stop ice from forming.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a power steering vehicle, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Check the hoses for leaks.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, when looking at the fifth wheel gap, you should:

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking a trailer coupling, make sure the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed tightly around the kingpin shaft, not the kingpin head.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: You will be asked to change lanes during the driving test. When the examiner asks you to do this, check traffic and use the proper signals before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The state will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: What do the two markings on a front brake limiting valve usually say?
questions.correctAnswerText: "Normal" and "slippery."
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve. It has two settings: "normal" and "slippery."

questions.question: How often should you inspect your cargo during a trip?

options.text: At the end of each day.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and its straps every time you take a break. You should also inspect it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you in a large vehicle, which should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you, increase your following distance and avoid quick moves. Do not speed up—the other driver will just tailgate you at a higher speed. Do not flash your brake lights either.

questions.question: How does an empty truck compare to a full truck when stopping?

options.text: It needs less distance to stop.
It needs more distance to stop.
It needs the same distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It needs more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer stopping distances than full trucks because they have less grip on the road.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve in a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about drivers behind a truck?

options.text: They may not see objects in front of the truck.
They usually have a clear view of the road ahead.
They do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not see objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your truck blocks the view of drivers behind you. They cannot see hazards in front of you. Flash your brake lights to warn them before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is the purpose of blocking a load?

options.text: It is only used for liquid cargo.
It keeps the load from moving during transport.
It is dangerous and should never be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps the load from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting while you are driving.

questions.question: What color are the malfunction lamps on vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps. They light up when the braking system is not working. Know where your lamp is before you start driving.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. In cold weather, water can freeze in the tanks and cause your brakes to fail.
